findings.area: canary observer side effect / callback cases
findings.summary: In callback-existing and nested-construct, captureState() resolves file:///audit/probe/fixtures/marker.txt through the installed userland resolver, which allow-lists marker.txt and returns fopen(). The userland external-entity-loader path is not gated by libxml_disable_entity_loader(true) in ext/libxml as far as static reading shows, so the after-kConf canary likely sees the marker; collect.validate() unconditionally requires not ev[1].marker_seen ('real kConf block') and would record a harness artifact as FAIL_RETAINED_OBSERVATIONS. Separately, the canary itself populates resolver_events, so 'pre-existing loader actually reached' is satisfied by the observer, not by SOAP/WSDL loading.
findings.fix_direction: Remove marker.txt from the resolver allow-list or make canary entity IDs distinct and recorded separately; tag resolver_events with $phase; require a good.wsdl/types.xsd/inner.wsdl system ID for the SOAP-reach claim; add case-specific (not universal) after-kConf expectations for callback cases, decided before execution.

findings.summary: captureState() overwrites global $phase and never restores it; diagnostics emitted during response decoding and afterCall after 'transport-enter-0' (and after 'transport-after-inner') are attributed to the transport phase. Evidence retained but mislabelled.

The 21 tests cover only bootstrap and FAIL_CASES fixtures for original/83. No synthetic fixture exercises POSITIVE result/transport_events, nested-*, callback cases, exp11 or runtime 74; F1 is not detectable by the suite.
findings.fix_direction: Add one synthetic fixture per remaining case family, including a callback-case after-kConf row.

findings.summary: On 8.3, libxml_disable_entity_loader() is deprecated (E_DEPRECATED per call, including kConf top-level and every before/afterCall) and kSoapClient::__call/__soapCall lack tentative return types; nested cases add stream_wrapper_restore notices and duplicate unregister warnings. They are retained (no @/filter) but the collector has no expected-diagnostic set, so a new/unexpected diagnostic class never fails a case.
findings.fix_direction: Optionally pin an expected diagnostic set per runtime/case, preserving unexpected ones as failures.
